summary: Mirdametinib (Gomekli) is an oral allosteric MEK1/MEK2 inhibitor for adults and children 2 years and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 who have symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas not amenable to complete resection. Dosing is body surface area based (2 mg/m2 twice daily, maximum 4 mg twice daily) on days 1 through 21 of each 28-day cycle, as capsules or tablets for oral suspension, with or without food. Key risks are ocular toxicity (retinal vein occlusion and pigment epithelial detachment), left ventricular dysfunction, dermatologic reactions, creatine phosphokinase elevation, neutropenia, and embryo-fetal toxicity. Baseline and periodic eye examinations and echocardiograms are required, with treatment held, reduced, or permanently stopped by severity.
indications: Treatment of adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) who have symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas not amenable to complete resection

admin: Give twice daily about 12 hours apart on days 1 through 21 of each 28-day cycle, then hold for 7 days; continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity
Capsules: swallow whole with or without food, one at a time if more than one is needed; do not open, break, or chew, and do not give to patients unable to swallow a whole capsule
Tablets for oral suspension: swallow whole with or without food, or disperse in drinking water and give as a liquid per the instructions for use
Complete baseline eye examination and echocardiogram before the first dose
If a dose is missed, or vomiting occurs after a dose, do not make it up; take the next scheduled dose at its regular time
moa: Mirdametinib is an allosteric inhibitor of mitogen-activated protein kinase kinases MEK1 and MEK2. By locking MEK in an inactive conformation it blocks MAPK pathway signaling downstream of RAS and RAF, reducing proliferation and survival of NF1-deficient plexiform neurofibroma cells driven by hyperactive RAS signaling.

monitor: Vision and eye examinations at baseline, at intervals, and for any new visual symptoms
Left ventricular ejection fraction by echocardiogram before starting, every 3 months in the first year, then as indicated
Skin for rash severity from the first signs
Creatine phosphokinase and neutrophil counts; pregnancy status before starting
relative: History of retinal vein occlusion, retinal pigment epithelial detachment, or glaucoma risk factors
Cardiac dysfunction or risk factors for reduced ejection fraction

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal findings, mirdametinib can cause fetal harm, including malformations and pregnancy loss. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 6 weeks after the last dose, and advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose. Mirdametinib may impair female fertility.
lact: It is not known whether mirdametinib passes into breast milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed child, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for mild or moderate renal impairment. Mirdametinib has not been studied in severe renal impairment; use with caution and monitor closely.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required for mild hepatic impairment. Moderate and severe hepatic impairment have not been evaluated; use with caution and monitor closely.

interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol during treatment as a general measure.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor creatine phosphokinase and neutrophil counts; assess ejection fraction by echocardiogram and perform ophthalmic examinations at baseline and during treatment.
interactions.food: Take with or without food; a high-fat meal lowers peak concentration without a meaningful change in total exposure.
major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers that also co-induce UGT, P-gp, and carboxylesterase enzymes (effect on mirdametinib exposure is unknown; avoid where possible)
minor: Does not inhibit CYP1A2, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, or 3A4 and does not induce CYP1A2, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, or 3A4.
moderate: Other drugs with ocular or cardiac toxicity (possible additive eye or ejection-fraction effects; monitor)

emergency: Sudden vision loss or severe visual change (possible retinal vein occlusion) - seek emergency eye care
Chest pain, severe breathlessness, or rapid swelling (possible cardiac dysfunction)
rare: Symptomatic ejection-fraction decline requiring permanent discontinuation
serious: Ocular toxicity including retinal vein occlusion and retinal pigment epithelial detachment
Left ventricular dysfunction with decreased ejection fraction
Severe dermatologic reactions including severe rash

monitoring: Comprehensive eye examinations before starting, at regular intervals, and promptly for any new or worsening visual change
Ejection fraction by echocardiogram before starting, every 3 months during the first year, then as clinically indicated
Skin examinations from the first signs of rash, with supportive care started early
Creatine phosphokinase and blood counts (neutrophils); pregnancy status in females of reproductive potential
counsel: Take your doses twice a day for the first 21 days of each 28-day cycle, then take no drug for 7 days; take with or without food
Report any vision change, blurred vision, or eye pain immediately, and keep all scheduled eye and heart (echocardiogram) visits
Report new shortness of breath, chest discomfort, swelling, unusual tiredness, severe rash, or muscle pain
Skin rash and diarrhea are common; start supportive skin care at the first signs and tell your team early

Use effective birth control during treatment and for 6 weeks (females) or 3 months (males with partners who could become pregnant) after the last dose; do not breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose
pk: Tumor volume reduction develops over months of cyclic treatment
Median time to peak about 1.1 hours for capsules and 0.8 hours for tablets for oral suspension
Mean terminal elimination half-life about 28 hours
Dosed on days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
Store capsules and tablets for oral suspension at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions 15-30 C (59-86 F) permitted; protect from light
pearls: Cyclic schedule is essential: 21 days on, 7 days off in every 28-day cycle; the week off is part of therapy
Dose is by body surface area with a 4 mg twice-daily ceiling; capsules and tablets for suspension are not interchangeable by handling (never open capsules)
Eye and heart monitoring are mandatory, not optional: baseline plus periodic exams catch RVO/RPED and ejection-fraction decline early
Rash and diarrhea are the most common reasons for dose holds; early supportive skin care keeps patients on therapy
High-fat food blunts the peak but not total exposure, so either fed or fasted dosing is acceptable if consistent
missed: If a dose of mirdametinib is missed, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose at its regular time. If vomiting occurs after a dose, do not take another dose; take the next scheduled dose at its regular time.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for mirdametinib overdose. Withhold the drug and provide supportive care with monitoring of cardiac function, vision, skin, creatine phosphokinase, and blood counts. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
